sections.html:
The Sangamon County Recorder is the official land records office for the county, and it permanently records deeds, mortgages, releases, assignments and liens. Its records go back to the early 1800s. It is a grantor and grantee office, meaning every record is found by the name of the seller or the buyer.

The office also stores subdivision plats, land surveys, veteran discharge papers and Uniform Commercial Code filings. Its job is to keep an accurate chain of title, which is the series of recorded documents that title companies review before a closing. The office is on the first floor of the County Building at 200 South Ninth Street in Springfield, and the main number is (217) 535-3150.

A standard deed costs $64 to record, and a non-standard document that carries the Rental Housing Support surcharge costs $84. State law HB3878 added $9.00 to the Rental Housing Support Fee in every Illinois county starting July 1, 2023.

Selected recording and copy fees
Document or serviceFee
Deed or mortgage on a standard 8.5 by 11 page$64
Non-standard document with surcharge$84
Standard document exempt from the surcharge$45
Non-standard document exempt from the surcharge$65
Plats 11 by 17$3 each

Plain copy$2 for two pages, $0.25 for each more

Judgments, powers of attorney, notices of probate and death certificates are among the items exempt from the surcharge. Accepted payment is cash, check or credit card. Checks are made payable to the Sangamon County Recorder.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Sangamon County sale
sections.html:
The transfer tax stamp rate is $0.50 per $500 of value for the state plus $0.25 per $500 of value for the county. A sale of $100 or more requires a PTAX-203, the real estate transfer declaration, to accompany the deed so the tax can be set from the sale price.

  • A gift is exempt from transfer tax, but the deed must contain the matching exemption paragraph.
  • Other transfers can qualify for exemption, and the recorder posts an exemption list.
  • Most deeds of record carry revenue stamps that show the sale price, which is how people look up what a home sold for.

Rely on the closing agent to calculate the exact stamp amount for your price, since it follows the printed rates above.

The deed needs to be prepared, signed and notarized, and it must carry the details the recorder requires for indexing. Document preparation can need legal knowledge, and staff cannot fill out forms or give legal advice, so an attorney is the person to consult.

  • The name and address of the preparer.
  • A return-to name and address.
  • A Tax Bill To name and address, if applicable.
  • The tax ID number and common address, which come from the Supervisor of Assessments at (217) 753-6805.
  • Black ink, on standard 8.5 by 11 paper with at least a 3 by 5 inch blank space in the upper right corner.

Documents are checked for statutory requirements and the fees are collected. They are recorded in the order received, given a document number, date and time, then scanned, indexed and verified.

You can bring it to the first-floor office, mail the original with a check for the exact fee, or have a title company use eRecording. Mail goes to the Sangamon County Recorder, 200 South 9th Street, First Floor, Springfield, IL 62701, with the return address included.

Mailed originals usually come back in three to five business days, and recorded documents can take up to seven to ten. Plan for the longer figure if a lender is waiting on the paperwork. eRecording, handled by approved vendors, cuts that to minutes and is mostly used by title companies, banks and law firms.

The online land records go back to 1982, deed books have been scanned to February 16, 1901, and older documents sit on microfiche in the office. Public terminals in the office are free.

The recorder sends the deed electronically to the Supervisor of Assessments, who updates the ownership record, usually within 4 to 6 weeks. The deed also tells that office where to mail future tax bills.

An owner has to tell the Supervisor of Assessments about a new mailing address in writing, by fax or in person, because telephone requests are not accepted. A name change needs supporting paperwork such as a court order or marriage license, and removing a name after a death needs a death certificate and a recorded document.

The recorder cannot perform title searches or give legal advice about liens. The office can only show you the records it holds, and staff recommend a title company for a full search and guarantee.

  • Lien records are checked in person at the recorder's office, not by phone.
  • A State tax lien question goes to the Illinois Department of Revenue State Tax Lien Unit at 217-785-5299.
  • For a federal tax lien, call 1-800-913-6050 for small business or self-employment liens and 1-800-829-7640 for wage or income liens.
  • An erroneous lien is a question for an attorney.

Lien releases are recorded with the office as well, and a seller who has paid off a lien should make sure the release is on record before closing. Call the recorder if you are unsure whether a lien or release is on file.

sections.h2: Before you record: a short checklist
sections.html:
Confirm the deed is signed and notarized, and that the preparer, return-to and Tax Bill To names and addresses are filled in. Get the tax ID number and common address from the Supervisor of Assessments. Attach the PTAX-203 if the sale is for $100 or more, and ask the closing agent for the stamp total. Bring a check for the exact fee made out to the Sangamon County Recorder, or let the title company send it through eRecording.

After recording, watch for the new owner's tax bill to arrive at the right address. If a bill from a past year surfaces, the County Clerk can say whether it was sold.

Sangamon County is built around Springfield, the state capital and county seat. It has an estimated 194,170 residents and 93,820 housing units, with 71.3% of occupied homes owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home value is $176,300, median gross rent is $983 and median household income is $75,357. Interstates 55 and 72 cross the county, and villages such as Chatham, Rochester, Riverton and Williamsville sit around Springfield.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Sangamon County Recorder?
faqs.a: It is on the first floor of the County Building, 200 South Ninth Street, Springfield, IL 62701. The main phone number is (217) 535-3150, and press 2 for document requirements. Mailed documents go to the same address.

faqs.q: How much is the Sangamon County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: A standard deed costs $64, and a non-standard document with the Rental Housing Support surcharge costs $84. Exempt documents cost $45 for standard and $65 for non-standard. Make checks payable to the Sangamon County Recorder.

faqs.q: Do I need a PTAX-203 to record a deed in Sangamon County?
faqs.a: Yes, if the transfer is a sale of $100 or more, a PTAX-203 must accompany the deed. A gift is exempt from transfer tax, but the deed must carry the exemption paragraph. The posted exemption list covers other qualifying transfers.

faqs.q: How long does Sangamon County take to return a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Plan on three to five business days for mailed originals, and up to seven to ten if the office is busy. eRecording through a title company can finish in minutes.

faqs.q: Are Sangamon County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes, data and images from 1982 forward are online, and deed books are scanned back to February 16, 1901. Some search options carry a charge, such as the Tapestry service, while a data-only search is free. Public terminals in the office are free to use.
